children: Portugal's centre-right minority government unveiled its 2027 budget bill on Thursday, projecting economic growth of 2.1% and a small fiscal surplus despite a number of tax cuts.
The bill submitted to parliament by Finance Minister Joaquim Miranda Sarmento sees the economy expanding at a slower pace than this year's projected 2.3%.

It aims for a budget surplus of 0.1% of GDP next year following a balanced budget in 2026, despite a new reduction in the general corporate tax rate to 18% from 19%, in line with the government's medium-term plan, tax cuts for lower-income households, and higher pension spending.
Parliament is due to vote on the bill in its first reading on October 28.
